paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you were born into a story you didn't pick, and Jesus rewrote the ending. Paul says sin entered the world through one man, and death was passed on to all men (Romans 5:12). That's heavy, and I won't pretend it isn't. But Paul isn't done, because he's only setting the table for what comes next.

Now watch what Paul does. He says "the gift is not like the trespass," and then he piles it on with "how much more" (Romans 5:15). One man's disobedience made the many sinners, and one man's obedience, Jesus Christ, will make the many righteous (Romans 5:19). Adam was a pattern of the One to come (Romans 5:14), and I'm a stamper, so I know a pattern when I see one, but this time the copy is BIGGER than the original! Even where sin increased, grace increased all the more (Romans 5:20).

So what do you do with that, baker? You stop trying to bake your way out of the hole, and you receive. Paul says those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through Jesus Christ (Romans 5:17). Sin reigned in death, but grace reigns through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord (Romans 5:21). That's not a cookie you earned, friend. It's a gift, and your hands are free to take it.
